attributes.body_ja:
「却って（かえって）」は、意図（いと）や期待（きたい）から外（はず）れた結果（けっか）を表（あらわ）すときによく使（つか）われる副詞（ふくし）です。「却（かえ）って」は、「(A)、却（かえ）って (B)」の形（かたち）で使（つか）われ、「(A) のつもりだったが、実際（じっさい）は (B)」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

「却（かえ）って」そのものは、「反対（はんたい）に」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。この表現（ひょうげん）は、話（はな）し手（て）は (A) を意図（いと）・期待（きたい）していたのに、(B) という反対（はんたい）の結果（けっか）になったというような場面（ばめん）で使（つか）われます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「却（かえ）って」に使（つか）われている漢字（かんじ）には、「却（しりぞ）く」（意味（いみ）：うしろに下（さ）がる）という読（よ）み方（かた）もあります。ここから、「(A) からうしろに下（さ）がってみたら、実際（じっさい）には (B) という結果（けっか）が見（み）えてくる」ようなイメージを持（も）つと良（よ）いかもしれません。
attributes.body:
In order to revoke, or take a step back from a statement that has already been made, 却（かえ）って will often be used. 却（かえ）って can translate as 'rather', or 'all the more'. If a sentence consists of '(A) 却（かえ）って, (B)', what it means is 'putting aside (A), (B)'. 却（かえ）って is an adverb.

却（かえ）って itself translates most closely to 'instead'. However, this is not the 'instead' used for phrases like '(B) was chosen over (A)', but the 'instead' used for phrases like '(A) couldn't be achieved, so (B)'. This shows that (A) is usually the intention or aim of the speaker, but (B) was the result instead.

Fun Fact

Another reading of the kanji used in 却（かえ）って is 却（しりぞ）く, which means 'to retreat'. This further highlights 却（かえ）って's nuance of 'stepping away' from the (A) statement, to show the real result of (B).

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both introduce unexpected outcomes, but differ in type of surprise. 却って means the result was the opposite of what was intended or expected, e.g. 謝ったら却って怒られた ('When I apologized, I was yelled at instead.') ところが highlights a surprising turn of events, though not necessarily the exact opposite, e.g. 田中さんに電話をかけた。ところがもう出発していた ('I called Tanaka. But he had already departed.')

attributes.body: Both むしろ and 却って  express contrast with expectation, but differ in nuance. むしろ introduces a preferred or clearer option, e.g. ワインよりむしろビールが飲みたい ('Rather than wine, I'd rather drink beer'). 却って highlights ironic reversal, e.g. 手伝ってあげたのに却って怒られた ('I helped, but they got angry instead').

attributes.body: 却って and 逆に both express something being counter to expectations, like the English 'on the contrary'. 却って is more formal, and occurs primarily in writing in the context of a full sentence or explanation. In contrast, 逆に is quite casual, and can be used in the same way as 却って, but also as an interjection at the beginning of a sentence or phrase, e.g. 逆にたかし君はどう思いますか？ ('On the contrary, what do you think, Takashi?').

first_relatable.title: 却って
first_relatable.meaning: All the more, On the contrary, Conversely

attributes.body: Both convey contradiction, but they differ in usage and nuance. 却って connects to the rest of the sentence to emphasize unexpected results, e.g. 慌てて出ようとしたら、却って遅くなった ('I tried to rush out, and I actually ended up running later.'). In contrast, に反して connects to a noun and highlights going against norms or expectations, e.g. 親の期待に反して、大学に進学しなかった ('Against his parents' expectations, he didn't go to college.').
